root_idea.summary: The root centers on testing and examination, especially an ordeal that reveals what is sound or unsound.
root_idea.development: The concrete image is assaying gold by fire. From this developed the senses of testing, affliction and punishment, and then related uses involving persecution, misguidance, conflict, and deviation.

senses.usage_conditions: In Quranic usage, the passive may describe being burned in the fire; the verb can also describe those who inflict such burning.

senses.definition: To try, test, or subject someone to an ordeal.
senses.usage_conditions: The ordeal may involve hardship, punishment, or circumstances through which a person's condition is revealed. Active and passive uses express causing or undergoing the test.

senses.definition: To turn someone away from the right course or revealed truth; to tempt or lead someone astray.
senses.usage_conditions: The Quranic construction may express an attempt to divert someone from what was revealed, or to induce deviation from the right way.

senses.definition: To subject people to persecution, affliction, or killing.
senses.usage_conditions: This is a Quranic use in which the affliction imposed by opponents is understood as persecution or, in certain cited interpretations, killing.

senses.definition: One who causes another to err or go astray from the truth.
senses.usage_conditions: In the Quranic construction بِفَاتِنِينَ عَلَيْهِ, the participle denotes those unable to lead the designated person astray except by the decree described in the verse.

senses.definition: A trial, test, or ordeal by which a person's condition is revealed.
senses.usage_conditions: The trial may come through hardship or prosperity, including circumstances involving wealth, children, or other worldly conditions; it is especially prominent in severe circumstances.
The noun may name the painful consequence or punishment produced by the ordeal, including punishment associated with fire.

senses.definition: Persecution, oppression, or slaughter inflicted on people.
senses.usage_conditions: This use describes affliction imposed by human opponents, especially when believers are persecuted or prevented from practicing their faith.

senses.definition: Conflict, civil strife, factional discord, or dissension.
senses.usage_conditions: The noun can denote a condition in which people form opposing factions or fall into violent communal conflict.

senses.definition: Unbelief or deviation from the right way.
senses.usage_conditions: In Quranic explanations of certain constructions, the noun denotes a state of religious deviation or unbelief rather than merely an external hardship.

senses.definition: Testing, trial, or a severe course of trying.
senses.usage_conditions: The form can convey a thorough or manifold process of testing rather than a single isolated test.

senses.definition: Afflicted, tried, or overwhelmed by a trial.
senses.usage_conditions: In the Quranic occurrence, the form is interpreted as a person afflicted or tested by fitna; it is a passive-participial use.

senses.definition: Madness or insanity; alternatively, one afflicted by madness.
senses.usage_conditions: This is a competing interpretation of the Quranic expression in which the form may be understood substantivally as the state of madness rather than simply as an afflicted person.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To melt or place gold or silver in fire in order to assay it and distinguish the good from the defective.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A concrete technical use associated with testing metal by fire.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To captivate, enamour, or induce admiration and pleasure.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of an influence that takes away a person's composure or reason and causes attachment.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To desire sexual intercourse or fornication.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized intransitive construction, including فَتَنَ إِلَى النِّسَاءِ and its passive counterpart.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The mutual or reciprocal causing of fitna, conflict, or discord with another.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A Form III verbal noun referring to the occasioning of fitna between parties.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To contend or wage war against one another.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Attested in the expression describing a group that continually quarrels in war.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A kind, sort, state, or condition; in the dual, the two end portions of the day.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The dual may refer to early morning and late evening because they are two distinct states or portions.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Burning with fire.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A concrete noun use referring to the act or condition of being burned.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The melting or assaying of gold and silver to separate the sound from the defective.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A technical use based on testing precious metal by fire.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Temptation, seduction, or a cause of being led astray.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: May refer to worldly display, desire, or another influence that attracts a person and exposes or endangers his condition.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Madness, insanity, or diabolical possession.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized state-of-affliction meaning distinct from ordinary testing or punishment.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A sin, crime, or act of disobedience deserving punishment.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A moral-legal extension of the noun's meaning.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Disgrace, shame, or ignominy.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A result or condition of being exposed to dishonor.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A cause of pleasure or satisfaction in another person, especially by giving that person grounds to feel superior.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A contextual and relational use, not a general synonym for every kind of trial.

other_classical_meanings.definition: In specialized expressions, the noun can designate whispering, being turned from the right road, questioning in the grave, a sword, or women.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: These are fixed or conventional collocations whose interpretation depends on the accompanying qualifier.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The mimosa farnesiana plant.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A botanical homonym or specialized later usage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A leather covering for a camel saddle.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Its plural is given as فُتُنٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Burnt; also, by comparison, black stones or a black stony tract resembling burned stone.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The stone and terrain uses are figurative extensions from the appearance of burning.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Short or small.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A dialectal Yemeni use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An intensive epithet for one who tests or tempts repeatedly or intensely.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The intensive form may function adjectivally or as a substantivized epithet.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A persistent tempter, specifically the devil.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A substantivized epithet for one who deceives people and embellishes disobedience.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A goldsmith or silversmith.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Named for the craftsman's melting and testing of precious metals.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A touchstone used to test gold and silver.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A feminine derivative referring to the testing stone.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Either of the two angels said to examine and question the dead in the grave.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Usually used in the dual expression فَتَّانَا الْقَبْرِ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A dirham and a dinar, regarded as things that test or tempt people.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used in the dual as a figurative designation of the two kinds of money.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A thief or robber who intercepts travelers on the road.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized occupational or descriptive use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a heart, fallen into a state of trial or affliction.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is the active-participle form derived from the intransitive use of فَتَنَ, not the Quranic transitive sense ‘causing another to err.’

other_classical_meanings.definition: A carpenter.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized lexical form with an irregular-looking pattern.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Burned or burnt.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A passive-participial use distinct from the Quranic interpretation of the occurrence as afflicted or mad.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Applied to gold or silver put into fire for assaying.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized description of tested precious metal.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A group of black camels collected together.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The designation is based on their resemblance in blackness to a burned or black stony tract.
